llm.summary: The skill is internally coherent: it's an instruction-only adapter for the CellCog cloud API that legitimately asks for a CELLCOG_API_KEY and python3; main user risks are uploading local files to an external service and optionally pip-installing an unreviewed SDK package.

dimensions.detail: Name/description promise Any-to-Any cloud service; declared requirements (python3, CELLCOG_API_KEY) and SKILL.md usage (CellCogClient, API calls) match that purpose. Nothing requests unrelated cloud providers, system-level credentials, or services outside CellCog.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to reference absolute local file paths in <SHOW_FILE> tags so CellCog can ingest them and to create tasks that deliver files/results back to the session. This is consistent with a multimodal cloud SDK, but it does mean local files and potentially sensitive data will be uploaded to the CellCog service—users should not send secrets or sensitive PII unless they trust CellCog's data handling.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the skill bundle (lowest risk). The docs suggest 'pip install cellcog' if the import fails; that's a normal SDK flow but means running code fetched from PyPI (or wherever the package comes from) at runtime. That is expected for an SDK but worth auditing before installing in high-security environments.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required, which is proportional to an API SDK. No unrelated credentials or system config paths are requested. Users should confirm the API key's scope and revoke/regenerate if it is shared or over-privileged.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable; it does not request elevated or persistent platform-wide privileges. Autonomous invocation remains enabled by default (normal), but no additional persistence or modifications to other skills are requested.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a straightforward SDK wrapper for the CellCog cloud service. Before using: (1) verify you trust https://cellcog.ai (check org, privacy/retention, and API key page); (2) avoid uploading sensitive secrets or PII in the <SHOW_FILE> paths unless you accept they will be sent to CellCog; (3) if you must install the 'cellcog' Python package, review its source/version on PyPI/GitHub first; (4) create and use a least-privilege API key and monitor credit and billing usage; (5) if you want to prevent autonomous agent calls to this service, disable or restrict the skill in agent settings—autonomous invocation is enabled by default but is platform-standard.
